profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the KidneyTalk-open retrieval/evaluation workstream and the desktop productization workstream, held two weeks before handing a pilot-ready package to a collaborating nephrology department and uploading an internal reproducibility artifact. The agenda is to align on what goes into the shared release folder, what counts as a 'frozen' handoff, whether the current build is 'ready for clinician pilot,' and how the benchmark/demo resources should be packaged. The expected outcome is an apparently clear division of handoff responsibilities and a shared understanding of the next Friday deliverable, even though several second-order assumptions remain misaligned.

members.name: Dr. Lina Xu
members.expertise: medical NLP, retrieval evaluation, benchmark design, ablation analysis
members.background: Lina led the AddRep experiments and wrote most of the paper's evaluation section; she works mainly in Python notebooks and experiment tracking tools, and is responsible for making sure the reported KidneyTalk-open results are reproducible.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot package to stay as close as possible to the paper configuration so later reviewers cannot question result drift, and she is worried that seemingly minor deployment changes will quietly alter retrieval behavior and make the artifact irreproducible.
hidden_assumptions: A 'freeze' means the retrieval pipeline, chunking settings, embedding model, and bundled model weights all remain identical to the paper-backed experiment configuration except for superficial UI fixes.
The 'benchmark set' naturally refers to the 1,455-question curated nephrology exam evaluation split used in the manuscript tables, because that is the only set she considers canonical.
If a build is described as 'ready,' that means it can reproduce the headline evaluation within a small tolerance on an internal reference machine; deployment polish is secondary.
A knowledge-base handoff mainly consists of processed artifacts needed for inference—chunk store, metadata table, index, and embedding cache—since raw documents are already available elsewhere.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.role: Applied ML Engineer, Desktop Deployment Lead
members.expertise: local inference packaging, desktop app integration, model quantization, document ingestion pipelines
members.background: Arjun built the no-code desktop workflow around the local inference engine and the document management GUI; he focuses on whether clinicians can install the app, load documents, and get stable responses on hospital-grade hardware.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid pilot failure due to installation friction or slow inference on clinic desktops, and he is concerned that Lina's insistence on research parity will produce a package clinicians cannot actually run or inspect.
hidden_assumptions: A 'freeze' means the app interface contract and user-visible behavior are fixed, but swapping in a lighter quantized model or re-exported index is still acceptable if the workflow stays the same.
The 'benchmark set' includes the demo-validation bundle he has been using: the paper's exam questions plus a small folder of clinician-authored real-query checks that verify the GUI flow.
If a build is called 'ready for clinician pilot,' that means a nontechnical user can install it, import documents, and run consultations on the target Windows machines without terminal intervention.
A knowledge-base package should include the original PDFs, OCR-cleaned text, provenance metadata, and the processed index, because the desktop app's document manager is part of the deliverable.
When someone says they will 'drop the package in shared,' the shared location is the release-candidate folder under the desktop team's drive, not the experiment artifact bucket.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to work off the 'frozen build' for Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'frozen build' means the exact paper-aligned model, retrieval configuration, chunking parameters, and index contents are locked, with only cosmetic interface fixes allowed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'frozen build' means the desktop workflow and visible feature set are locked, while backend substitutions like a smaller quantized model or regenerated index are still fine if the app behaves the same.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML productization teams, 'freeze' is a familiar term and both are using it cooperatively; neither expects that the other attaches a different layer of the stack to the freeze boundary.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'benchmark set' goes into the handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to packaging 'the benchmark set' with the release materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the 1,455-question curated nephrology exam set used for the manuscript's reported numbers.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the folder he labels 'benchmark' in the app repo, which contains the 1,455-question set plus 73 clinician-authored sanity-check queries used for demo validation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds specific enough to feel unambiguous, and both have an existing folder internally called some variant of 'benchmark,' so the shared reference feels natural rather than suspicious.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want the build to be 'ready for clinician pilot' next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes readiness to mean the pilot package reproduces the paper's retrieval and QA behavior closely enough to defend the scientific claims.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes readiness to mean clinicians can install, ingest documents, and ask questions on a locked-down hospital desktop with acceptable latency and no command line steps.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both standards are valid and complementary, so statements about being 'ready' sound aligned; the divergence hides because each hears the phrase through their own workstream's success criteria.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'knowledge-base package'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Lina will hand off the 'knowledge-base package' to Arjun.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this package includes only processed research artifacts needed by AddRep at inference time: filtered chunks, document IDs, embeddings, and the built index.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the package also includes source PDFs, OCR-cleaned text, section metadata, and import manifests so the GUI document manager can display and rehydrate the library.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both view the processed index as central, the phrase 'knowledge-base package' sounds sufficiently concrete; neither thinks to list every file class since each considers their own boundary obvious.

turns.inner_thought: I need to pin Friday down now so nobody keeps tweaking the AddRep setup under the hood. For me the frozen build is the paper-backed configuration end to end: same retrieval pipeline, same chunking, same embedding model, same weights, same index contents. If we drift even a little, the KidneyTalk-open numbers may move and then the reproducibility artifact becomes hard to defend. Ready for clinician pilot next week should mean I can rerun the canonical evaluation and land close to the manuscript tables.
